text: Novo Nordisk’s Alzheimer’s trial failure triggered a sharp market purge event, exposing a major function misalignment. The company’s attempt to expand semaglutide from metabolic regulation into cognitive trajectory control was structurally rejected, resulting in a four-year share-price low, accelerated investor outflow, and reinforcement of core-function boundaries. The field executed a correction sequence—freeze, wipe, rewrite, install—forcing Novo back to its obesity/diabetes domain and punishing non-resonant expansion. This registers as a high-magnitude pre–Cycle-8 purge signal, with inversion effects visible in competitor strength (LLY) and Novo’s leadership overhaul.
